items.headline: 30-year bond auction ($25bn, 11-12): high yield 5.441%, 0.4 bp tail vs WI 5.437% (largest 30-year tail since June), bid-to-cover 2.36 (Oct 2.54; six-auction avg 2.44), indirects 68.1% (Oct 72.3%), directs 20.5%, dealers 11.4% (Oct 6.8%) - 'softest demand in five months'; all three refunding auctions weaker than October
items.source: helious.io auction results page (11-12 18:05 UTC); Gokhshtein Media (11-12 18:27 UTC); Seeking Alpha via TradingView (11-12); bloomingbit (11-12); HERE Rock Hill (11-13 06:24 ET); all read by WebFetch
items.claim: The Treasury sold $25bn of 30-year bonds (5.375% coupon, due Nov 2056) on 2026-11-12 at a high yield of 5.441%, 0.4 bp above the 5.437% when-issued yield - a small tail that Gokhshtein calls the largest for the maturity since June, and the second tail of the week after the 10-year's 1.0 bp on 11-10. Bid-to-cover fell to 2.36 from 2.54 at the October reopening (six-auction average 2.44) on about $59bn of bids; indirects took 68.1% versus 72.3% in October (average 70.5%), directs 20.5% (Oct 20.9%), and primary dealers were left with 11.4% versus 6.8% in October (average 9.5%). The high yield was below October's 5.618% because of the intervening price rally, not stronger demand; HERE Rock Hill calls it the softest demand in five months and says all three refunding auctions (3-year 2.53 b/c, 10-year 5.020%/2.46 b/c, 30-year 2.36) showed investors reluctant to add long-term debt. helious.io's own verdict is 'IN LINE'. The 30-year closed near 5.43% and the 10-year near 5.10-5.13%, its highest in three weeks.
items.note: Tail of 0.4 bp is below the 2 bp hard-event threshold. Five sources agree on 5.441% / 2.36 / 68.1% / 20.5%; WI 5.437% from Gokhshtein, Seeking Alpha and bloomingbit; dealer 11.4% and Oct 6.8% from helious.io and HERE Rock Hill. investinglive wrap ('tails as demand disappoints for second straight day') could not be fetched (server error).

items.candidate_dial: capex cut/deferral/digestion (neocloud: NBIS) - revenue/capacity DEFERRAL into 1H27; capex RAISED, not cut
items.claim: Nebius reported Q3 2026 revenue of $980.8m (+571% y/y), adjusted EBITDA $465.8m, Q3 capex $7.30bn ($15.43bn nine months), cash $7.4bn and non-current debt $14.0bn, and raised 2026 capex to approximately $27bn, 'above our $20-25 billion range', with 2027 capex guided at $40-45bn for more than 1 GW of new capacity (prepayments and asset-backed financing of investment-grade contracts such as Microsoft and Meta expected to cover 75-85%; committed customer prepayments ~$10bn in 2026 rising to $17-20bn in 2027). But 2026 revenue is now guided to the low end of the $3.0-3.4bn range (TechCrunch: a ~$200m cut to ~$3bn) with part of this year's revenue moving into early 2027, and the December ARR target of $7-9bn becomes '>$7bn for February', about a two-month shift, because 'where we rely on third parties, there have been delays' and 'delivery dates at a number of colocation sites shifted into the first half of 2027'; at the New Jersey DataOne site the operator retired temporary generation in late Q3 ahead of permanent power, resetting the remaining tranches to 2Q27, and just over half of the Microsoft capacity (contract up to $19.4bn) is now planned by year-end with the rest in Q2 2027. CEO Volozh: 'Building at this scale is hard, and delays are part of our industry right now... We are not immune'; the letter says 'shifts in colocation timelines do not reflect structural change' and that contracts remain in place. 2027 revenue guided $12-13bn with pre-tax breakeven targeted Q4 2027; contracted power >4 GW (target 5 GW by year-end). Shares fell 16-18% on 11-12 (CNBC -16%; TechCrunch -17%; Cuviliez -18%).
items.note: Partial by the same rule as CoreWeave 11-10: capex number went UP (not a cut), so the hit is the dated capacity/revenue deferral and the 'delays' language, plus the Microsoft-delivery slip that follows Bloomberg's 11-05 report of Microsoft tightening neocloud oversight (prior). No 'digestion' word used. Shareholder letter read to 100,000 of 107,692 characters; investing.com transcript rate-limited; convergedigest failed.

items.candidate_dial: pulled/downsized deal (potential: Nvidia vendor-finance backstop for OpenAI) - pushback reported, nothing pulled
items.claim: The Information reported on 2026-11-12 (sources) that Colette Kress, elevated to interim CEO after Jensen Huang's resignation, 'has sometimes pushed back on deals that Huang championed' and 'may take a more conservative approach', the cited example being a proposed $250bn credit backstop on OpenAI's behalf that would have let OpenAI fill eight gigawatts of data-center space with Nvidia's newest chips. Neither write-up says the backstop was cancelled: Nvidia split the proposal into two parts in August and guaranteed about $100bn for the first part (AI Weekly's tally lists a $105bn guarantee tied to OpenAI's Ohio campus, $36bn of neocloud cloud purchases, $20bn of data-center leases and up to $125bn behind a Wall Street credit programme, ~$286bn in all, citing FinanceFeeds); TokenPost adds that 'some cloud deals were cancelled as data center projects faced delays' without naming them. Cuviliez (11-13, citing Fortune) frames it as neocloud and GPU-backed debt models likely losing an implicit Nvidia backstop. Huang's resignation date is not given in either page; Huang reportedly agreed to testify to Congress before Thanksgiving and a DOJ antitrust probe is ongoing.
items.note: Partial: a reported change of stance on vendor financing, not a pulled or downsized deal. Figures are secondhand (The Information via aggregators; FinanceFeeds tally). Relevant to the capex-credit fuse because Nvidia guarantees sit behind OpenAI/neocloud financing; the next quarterly disclosure is the check.

items.claim: Trading Economics reports the UK 10-year gilt yield above 5.3% on 2026-11-13, its highest since late October, and the 2-year above 5%, its highest since October 2023, after the 10-year had steadied around 5.2% on 11-11 following the prior session's selloff and risen toward 5.3% on 11-12 from more-than-two-month lows. Drivers given are stronger-than-expected UK GDP (Q3 +0.7% q/q, +1.9% y/y; September +0.2%), markets pricing over an 80% chance of a December Bank of England hike (from 50% at the start of the week) and three more by mid-2027 after the November hike, Deputy Governor Lombardelli's warning of possible consecutive hikes, and strong US inflation data lifting Treasury yields. Bloomberg's 11-13 live blog is headlined 'Gilts head for worst week since September' and its 11-11 newsletter 'UK gilts get pulled into US bond selloff' (neither fetched). No 30-year gilt level or gilt-Bund spread is reported on the fetched page; the prior run recorded 30y at 5.65% on 11-11 (leprivatebanker).
